title: Micro rollout safety cheats (personal journal)
content:
Purpose:
- Quick personal checklist and heuristic bank for tiny staged rollouts (1% -> 10% -> 25% -> 100%) when I'm the oncall/planner. Not a formal runbook, more a pragmatic cheat sheet for low-risk incremental pushes.

High-level constraints I keep in mind:
- Prefer shorter canary windows for stateless endpoints (10-15m) and longer for anything with persistent state or cache-warming implications (30-60m).
- Avoid model swaps that change tokenization or output shape at <25% traffic unless rollback is trivial.
- Always have a fallback model image/variant pinned and tested under load prior to any rollout.

Quick preflight (10m):
1) Confirm health endpoints green across 3 AZs.
2) Smoke generate 10 prompts with the exact model variant and compare diffs vs baseline.
3) Check KV cache metrics (hit rate, memory) — ensure no sudden drop-in or spike.
4) Validate tracing is sampling at >=1% and traces contain model-version tag.
5) Ensure alert channel is set (pager/team Slack).

Fast abort criteria (auto/manual):
- Latency P95 increases > 50% AND error rate >= 0.5% above baseline for 3 consecutive windows (5m).
- Production error rate (4xx+5xx) increases by absolute 0.3% and sustained for 2 windows.
- Model hallucination-related metric (customer-facing QA metric) regression > 8% on sentinel prompts.
- Sudden drop in token throughput with no resource changes (possible deadlocks).
- Prefix-caching eviction rate increases > 20% leading to cold-start amplification.

Observability queries I run (quick snippets to paste into Obs):
- request_rate by model,region last 30m
- p50,p95,p99 latency by model_version where model_version in (candidate,baseline)
- error_rate{status>=400} by model_version split by AZ
- cache_hit_ratio by model_name (look for dips)
- user-facing QA false_positive_rate for sentinel set (run evaluation pipeline)

Manual intervention checklist (if noisy signals but unsure):
- Roll traffic back 50% immediately and hold.
- Trigger a targeted smoke run against the rolled-back variant comparing identical prompts.
- If possible, route a small set of verbose debug requests to a canary instance (enable extra debug headers).
- If root cause unclear after 25m, escalate to runtime/infra and pause further rollout.

Traffic steering tips (my shorthand):
- Use sticky cookies for session fidelity when comparing behavior across versions.
- For large customers, prefer cohort pinning (users with >X monthly tokens) and validate directly rather than blind percentage.
- Gradual leaps: 1% -> 5% -> 15% -> 50% -> 100% only if all signals are stable at each step for the configured min_window.

Version pinning notes:
- Always preserve an immutable alias (e.g., stable-v2025-02-10) before pushing new variant.
- When updating alias, keep previous image for at least 2 * max TTL of caches used in that release to allow rollback without cache poisoning.
- Document config diffs: tokenization, max_seq, quantization flags, attention kernel hints. Small changes in these can explain latency shifts.

Post-rollback forensic checklist (what I do within first 2 hours):
- Snapshot candidate and baseline logs (request/response pairs) for the period surrounding the anomaly.
- Run the sentinel prompt suite on both stacks and dump model outputs to S3 for diffing.
- Check infra metrics: GPU memory pressure, kernel time, stalls, and host-level cgroup throttling.
- Talk to whoever touched packaging/quantization in the last 48h — sometimes a CI change slips through.

Low-cost safety levers I rely on:
- Prefetch & cache priming for warmup: send small warmup traffic to canary instances before shifting real user traffic.
- Response size cap: enforce server-side token limits on canary to limit worst-case token costs.
- Burst shaper: cap per-client QPS to avoid a noisy neighbor from skewing canary stats.

Small operational reminders (notes to self):
- Remember to run quick evals in the same region as the canary to avoid cross-region latency noise.
- If using quantized variant, compare output token-by-token for stop-sequence behavior — quant changes sometimes add spurious tokens.
- Keep a tiny list of 8–12 sentinel prompts per vertical (search, chat, assistant) that are cheap but indicative.

Open questions / things to refine later:
- Should we default to longer windows for any model change that touches tokenizer? (leaning yes)
- Automate a lightweight canary health dashboard that computes a rolling composite score I can glance at.
- Add a column in release metadata that calls out expected cache warmup penalty and estimated cost delta.

Random commands I always forget and paste here:
- \"kubectl rollout undo deployment/model-serving --to-revision=<rev>\"
- query for p95: graphsql/metrics: sum(rate(requests_total{handler=\"generate\",model=~\".*\"}[5m])) by (model_version)
- S3 dump path: s3://redwood-release-dumps/<date>/candidate-vs-baseline/

Final quick checklist before sleep after a rollout:
- Confirm alias rollback path tested and one person owns it for next 2 hours.
- Notify product/CS of percentage and any expected ephemeral regressions.
- Leave this file pointer in Slack thread for follow-ups.

-- end of scratchpad (a living doc)

Notes to self: keep this short, prune after 3 experiments, move repeated items to the central runbook once stable.
